items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: The transcript quotes Mezzrow's book stating Joe Sullivan agreed to join a band, but the interviewer explicitly notes 'you may not have been around' and the interviewee does not confirm personal participation or acquaintance.

ctx.x: He says in August of 1933 he signed a contract with a financial backer to support a mixed Big Band, which had Alex Hill, as the arranger, to front it. This is in Mezzrow's Mezra's book.

He said "The following agreed to join: Joe Sullivan, Bud Freeman, Floyd O'Brien, Max Kaminsky, Gene Krupa, Eddie Condon and Pee Wee Russell. We rehearsed and the future looked good and we were okay for a sustaining program on a network, but soon after, the men in the band left him to go to a rehearsal arranged by Red McKenzie for some other guy who claimed he was a politician's son ..."
Do you remember any of these details? I mean you may not have been around ...
